## Purpose

Fixes #42210.

When streaming auto tool parsing ends before a valid tool-call delta is emitted, vLLM can drop parser-buffered raw text and incorrectly finish as `tool_calls`. This PR flushes the buffered suffix as plain assistant `content` whenever generation reaches a terminal finish before a tool call is streamed, preserving the engine's original `finish_reason`, such as `stop` or `length`.

If a real tool-call delta has already been streamed, the response still finishes as `tool_calls`.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -q -k "streaming_tool_parser_flushes_buffered_content_on_terminal_finish or streaming_tool_parser_stop_flush_skips_streamed_content or streaming_tool_parser_does_not_flush_after_tool_call_delta or has_unstreamed_tool_parser_state_handles_non_integer_tool_ids"
```

## Test Result

```text
6 passed, 38 deselected
pre-commit hooks passed
```

nice fix. two questions to make sure i'm reading the new code right:

1. **`streamed_content_lengths[i]` accounting.** I see the init (`streamed_content_lengths = [0] * num_choices` at the top of the generator) but couldn't find where it gets incremented when an actual content delta is sent earlier in the stream. if it stays at `0` throughout the run and a content delta IS emitted before the requested stop fires, then `previous_texts[i][streamed_content_lengths[i] :]` would re-emit the already-streamed prefix as the final delta. is the increment happening somewhere I missed, or is the assumption that this code path only triggers when no content has been streamed yet (so 0 is fine)?

2. **`_has_unstreamed_tool_parser_state` portability.** the check looks scoped to parsers that buffer state in `prev_tool_call_arr` / `streamed_args_for_tool` (llama3_json, hermes-style). would a parser that buffers in a different shape (e.g. raw-text accumulator instead of partial-JSON-tool-call tracker) silently miss this code path? worth a docstring on the helper noting the buffer-shape contract so future parsers know they need to opt in (or expose a generic flush hook).

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request ensures that when a streaming chat completion is interrupted by a requested stop reason during tool parsing, any buffered text is flushed as content and the finish_reason is correctly preserved as "stop". This aligns streaming behavior with non-streaming behavior and includes a new test case for verification. However, a critical issue was identified where using the accumulated text buffer for the final flush could lead to content duplication in the streaming response, as it doesn't account for text already emitted in previous chunks.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `previous_texts[i]` here will cause content duplication in the streaming response if any content was already emitted for this choice in previous chunks. `previous_texts[i]` is an accumulated string of all text generated so far. When flushing the buffer at the end of the stream, only the portion of the text that has not yet been sent to the client should be included in the `delta_message`. To fix this, track the length of the text already emitted for each choice and only send the remaining suffix from `previous_texts[i]`.

Using `previous_texts[i]` here will cause content duplication in the streaming response if any content was already emitted for this choice in previous chunks. `previous_texts[i]` is an accumulated string of all text generated so far. When flushing the buffer at the end of the stream, only the portion of the text that has not yet been sent to the client should be included in the `delta_message`. To fix this, track the length of the text already emitted for each choice and only send the remaining suffix from `previous_texts[i]`.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request ensures that when a streaming chat completion is interrupted by a requested stop reason during tool parsing, any buffered text is flushed as content and the finish_reason is correctly preserved as "stop". This aligns streaming behavior with non-streaming behavior and includes a new test case for verification. However, a critical issue was identified where using the accumulated text buffer for the final flush could lead to content duplication in the streaming response, as it doesn't account for text already emitted in previous chunks.
The new parser engine already handles this case. However, Llama has not yet been migrated to the new parser. Could you retest this with Qwen3?
